summary: Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied under Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of California in 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2010).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Komarovski studied at Dzongsar Institute, Palyul Chokhorling, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of Virginia. He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (attested 2011).

Yaroslav Vassilkov (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1960–1967). He held posts at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (~1967–1993), Kunstkamera (~1993), and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta. He was later an emeritus professor at Komazawa University.

Yasuhiko Nagano (born 1946) is a linguist and Tibetologist. Educated at TUFS, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1983), he served as a professor and professor emeritus at the National Museum of Ethnology, among other academic executive roles.
Yasuhiko Sueki (born 1952) is a scholar in philosophy and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1971 to 1980. He became an emeritus professor at Komazawa University around 2018.

Yasuhiro Okazaki specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Hiroshima University, where he studied under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and later held teaching posts at several prefectural high schools, including Takamiya High School.

Yasuhiro Sueki (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He held posts at Kyoto University and served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1976–2000).

Yasuke Ikari (born 1940) is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University under Masaaki Hattori and earned a PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught extensively at Kyoto University, serving as assistant professor, professor, and later professor emeritus in 2004.

Yasumasa Sekine (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at the Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS University of London, he held professorships at Japan Women's University (~2000–2013) and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2013–2018).

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He subsequently taught there as an assistant, associate professor, and full professor from 1966 until 1999.

Yasuo Deguchi (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After doctoral studies at Kyoto University, he became an associate professor and then professor there, later serving as Dean of Letters and founding the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy in 2023.

Yasuo Goto is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Yasuo Inamoto (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum from ~1995 to 2007 before taking up a post at Kyoto University in ~2007.

Yasuo Matsunami (1948–2010) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano and later served as a lecturer there (attested 1992–2006) and advisor to the Sravakabhumi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
